args.code:
# Reverse the XOR-based validation algorithm
# edx starts at 0x66 ('f')
# For each position i: input[i] XOR edx == expected[i]
# Then edx = edx + input[i]

# Expected bytes at 0x402060
expected = bytes([0x20, 0xe0, 0xb9, 0x7e, 0xfb, 0x8e, 0x1e, 0xac, 
                  0x63, 0xb7, 0xd4, 0x72, 0xb6, 0xd4, 0x74, 0xb7,
                  0xe8, 0x71, 0x49, 0xc5, 0x16, 0x25])

# Reverse: input[i] = expected[i] XOR edx
edx = 0x66  # Initial value
result = []

for i in range(22):
    char = expected[i] ^ (edx & 0xff)  # Keep only low byte of edx
    result.append(char)
    edx = (edx + char) & 0xffffffff  # edx is 32-bit

password = bytes(result)
print(f"Password (bytes): {password}")
print(f"Password (string): {password.decode('latin-1')}")

# Verify
edx = 0x66
for i in range(22):
    c = password[i]
    xored = c ^ (edx & 0xff)
    print(f"i={i}: char={chr(c) if 32<=c<127 else hex(c)}, edx&0xff={edx&0xff:02x}, xored={xored:02x}, expected={expected[i]:02x}, match={xored==expected[i]}")
    edx = (edx + c) & 0xffffffff
